h1: New Siya Hotel — a budget hotel with a pool, right in central Talat Maha Sarakham
intro: If you want somewhere inexpensive but still right in the city centre, walkable to the market and temples, with a pool to cool off in, New Siya Hotel is a newer 3-star hotel on Somthawinrat Road in the Talat area of central Maha Sarakham that fits the bill nicely · It's a small, friendly hotel with an outdoor pool, a spa/massage room, a restaurant, free parking and a 24-hour front desk — well suited to travellers, business guests or small families who want a central stay without paying a lot · Rooms start at around THB 650/night, and real guest reviews give it about 8.4, praising mainly the clean rooms and the lovely staff.

body.html: New Siya Hotel sits on Somthawinrat Road in the Talat subdistrict of Mueang Maha Sarakham — a small, newer hotel right in the city's central market area · What guests like most is the location: it's an easy walk to temples and markets, close to the night market (walking street), Wat Nakwichai and Wat Mahachai, so heading out for food, temple visits or an evening stroll is simple, with no need to drive anywhere far.

Rooms come in several styles, from Standard up to Deluxe Twin and Suite rooms for couples or a small family · all rooms have air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a private bathroom with a rainfall shower, and free Wi-Fi · many reviews say the rooms are larger than expected for the price, clean and tidy, with comfortable beds — good for an overnight stop on the road or a trip into town for business.
"The rooms are clean and tidy, the staff and housekeepers are very lovely, and the location is great — near shopping, restaurants and temples, easy to get around."

What guests mention most is the cleanliness of the rooms and how friendly the staff are, along with the outdoor pool that's handy for cooling off, and the in-house spa/massage room · there's an on-site restaurant, free private parking, a lift, and a 24-hour front desk that can store luggage · between the central location and the reachable price, it stands out as a strong pick for anyone who wants to stay in the middle of Maha Sarakham without spending much.

To be honest about it — this is a budget hotel; the facilities are adequate rather than luxurious · some reviews note the TV only gets a few channels and the shower water runs slowly in a few rooms, both common at this level · another point is that prices on some platforms can be higher than the walk-in rate at the counter, so it's worth comparing channels before you book · if you set your expectations to the price and the budget 3-star level, these are easy enough to live with.

In short, New Siya Hotel suits travellers, business guests or a small family who want a central stay in Maha Sarakham, walkable to the market and temples, with a pool, at an easy price · it's not for those after a luxury resort or a riverside-nature setting, but if you want a clean room, a central location, free parking and a pool to dip into, it delivers all that on a comfortable budget — and the reviews confirm most guests come away happy.

A tip from reading the reviews: always compare the direct or walk-in rate against the platforms first, as the walk-in price is sometimes cheaper · if you're coming as a family, ask about a Suite or Deluxe Twin that sleeps more · if you want to use the pool, check its opening hours, and pick an upper-floor room if you'd rather avoid street noise from the market area.

faqTitle: FAQ — New Siya Hotel, Maha Sarakham

faq.q: Where is New Siya Hotel in Maha Sarakham?
faq.a: It sits on Somthawinrat Road in the Talat subdistrict of Mueang Maha Sarakham, right in the city's central market area · it's a walk to Wat Nakwichai (~290 m), the night market (~840 m) and Wat Mahachai (~1 km), and about a 5-minute drive from Mahasarakham University.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 650/night for a Standard room · there's a Deluxe Twin around THB 750 and a Suite Double around THB 950 · prices vary by season and booking channel, so compare platforms and message the hotel for the direct rate before booking.

faq.q: Is there a pool? Is there a spa too?
faq.a: Yes — there's an outdoor swimming pool and an in-house spa/massage room · check the pool's opening and closing hours first so you can plan your swim time.

Yes — there's free private parking and an on-site restaurant, plus a 24-hour front desk that can store luggage · ask about breakfast options when you book · handy for those who drive in and want a central stay.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers, business guests or a small family who want a central stay in Maha Sarakham, walkable to the market and temples, with a pool, at an easy price · less suited to those after a luxury resort or a riverside-nature setting outside town.

faq.q: How are the review scores, and any cautions?
faq.a: Real guest reviews give it about 8.4, strong on clean rooms, lovely staff and the central location · the main cautions are that it's a budget hotel with adequate facilities, the TV in some rooms gets only a few channels, and prices on some platforms can run above the walk-in rate.
